validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: confirmed and correctly classified. This is FGT's real Phase VI Expansion Project, FERC Docket No. CP02-27-000, certificate application filed Nov 15, 2001 (Federal Register notice 66 FR 59584, https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2001/11/29/01-29619/...). Independently corroborated by Oil & Gas Journal (two separate articles: the Nov 15, 2001 announcement 'Florida Gas Transmission to add capacity to Texas-to-Florida line', and the May 15, 2003 construction-progress piece 'Florida Gas Transmission completes Phase V expansion, begins Phase VI'). GEM's row is the WHOLE Phase VI project as one segment/row (not a duplicate of any other roster PID) -- the FERC notice's itemized facility list sums to the sheet's length: Mainline Expansions = 5.3 mi of 36-in loop (Baldwin & Mobile Counties, AL) + 20.1 mi of 30-in loop (Bradford, Clay, Suwannee, Washington Counties, FL); Other Expansions = 1.3 mi of 6-in lateral loop (Lake Co, FL) + 1.4 mi of 16-in lateral extension (Brevard Co, FL) + 5.2 mi of 16-in lateral off the 26-in Stanton Lateral (Orange Co, FL). Total = 33.3 mi, matching GEM's LengthKnown=33.0 mi almost exactly. Capacity: FERC notice states 121,000 Dth/d summer peak (85,356 Dth/d average annual) -- matches GEM's Capacity=121.00 MMcf/d. Cost: FERC notice states '$105.4 million'; OGJ (both articles) round to '$105 million'; GEM's SegmentCost=105,000,000 USD is the rounded OGJ figure -- consistent, not material (0.4% variance, both describe the identical project scope). StartYear1=2003: FERC notice targets deliveries commencing June 1, 2003 and remaining facilities operational Nov 1, 2003; OGJ's May 2003 article confirms construction was under way toward those same phased in-service dates -- confirmed, tier=high, 2 independent sources (FERC/Federal Register + trade press). SPEC CAVEAT -- Diameter: GEM records only '36' but the FERC notice shows this single Phase VI Project row actually comprises FOUR different pipe diameters (36-in AL mainline loop, 30-in FL mainline loop, 16-in FL laterals x2, 6-in FL lateral). 36-in is not wrong (it is one of the diameters used, and is the largest), but it is incomplete versus GEM's own convention elsewhere on this sheet of listing all diameters present in a multi-size build (compare sibling rows P4035 '16, 24, 36' and P4037 '16, 24, 36'). Recommend appending 30, 16, 6. Owner1='Florida Gas Transmission Co LLC' 100% (already staged as MISSING_REF, not MISSING_VALUE) is correct: this is the direct legal owner of record per FERC's own application ('Florida Gas Transmission Company... filed an application...') and PHMSA's operator registry (Operator ID 5304, 'FLORIDA GAS TRANSMISSION CO'); deeper ownership runs through Citrus Corp, a 50/50 Kinder Morgan / Energy Transfer joint venture, per Wikipedia and general search -- noted but not restated at the Owner1 level since GEM's Owner1 already correctly names the direct holding entity. Opened and read to exhaustion: FERC Federal Register notice (full text), both OGJ articles, Wikipedia FGT article, PHMSA operator record. No duplicate/relabel risk found against the 37-row roster -- no other roster PID's length/diameter/location profile overlaps this 33-mile, mixed-diameter, AL+FL loop-and-lateral package.

FGT is a long-haul interstate mainline that receives gas at numerous interconnects along its Texas-Louisiana-Mississippi-Alabama-Florida route (Transco, Tennessee Gas Pipeline, Gulf South, Gulfstream, and others), not a single named upstream field/plant -- no single FuelSource is attributable to a mainline capacity-expansion phase like this one. Left blank per the FuelSource gotcha (never default to 'Natural Gas'; leave blank rather than guess a facility).
